title: Wayve employees cash in shares worth $85m

Wayve, the Cambridge autonomous driving startup, and Uber are partnering to put robotaxis on the streets of London later this year. Wayve has raised $2.8 billion and the value of the shares sold by employees was based on the company’s latest valuation of $8.5 billion. Crowdcube, the private market investment platform, managed the share sales. It was also the largest transaction under the FCA’s PISCES (Private Intermittent Securities and Capital Exchange System) regulation to date. Dame Julia Hoggett, LSE CEO, said: “We are delighted to see the PISCES framework and our Private Securities Market being utilised by innovative companies, such as Wayve, seeking liquidity events for their stakeholders, including employees.” “This is the first of what we hope will be many of these transactions with partners using our infrastructure to manage complex employee liquidity transactions on the PSM,” said Crowdcube CEO Matt Cooper. Crowdcube says it is seeing an increase in the number of companies looking to complete secondary share sales which provide liquidity for employees and early stage investors. This is the second time in Wayve’s history that it has provided staff with a way to monetise their equity. The first was via a tender offer for employee shares during its Series C funding round in 2024. See all our Automotive content .
